name: analyze_capacity
description: Analyze system capacity utilization and trends for capacity planning. Provides utilization percentages, growth rates, and projections based on historical metrics. Includes CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O analysis.

time_range.description: Historical time range for trend analysis (default: MONTH, about 30 days; note the get_*_metrics tools default to HOUR). The range used is returned as time_range in each section

name: apply_update
description: Apply downloaded TrueNAS system update. System will reboot if reboot parameter is true. Supports dry-run mode to preview changes. Returns a task ID for tracking progress. This is a write operation. **Best Practice**: After successful update and reboot, use query_boot_environments to check for old boot environments that can be safely pruned with delete_boot_environment. Recommend keeping 2-3 recent boot environments for rollback safety. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

reboot.description: Reboot after update completes (default: false for safety)

name: check_updates
description: Check for available TrueNAS system updates. Returns allow-listed fields for each available version (train, version, release notes and URL).

name: configure_directory_service
description:
Configure and join a directory service (Active Directory, LDAP, or IPA) with TrueNAS directoryservices.update (TrueNAS 25.10 or later). Setting enable=true joins the domain automatically the first time. The arguments are the fields of that API call. Omitted optional fields keep their current value.

**To enable or change a service, service_type, credential, configuration and enable are all required, and configuration must match service_type. The old flat arguments (type, server, bindname, netbiosname, ssl, domain, ...) no longer exist: put them in credential and configuration as below.**

**To disable the configured service, send only enable=false** (no service_type, credential or configuration): the settings are kept and domain authentication stops until it is enabled again. When service_type is sent with enable=false, a KERBEROS_USER credential is rejected for ACTIVEDIRECTORY and IPA (TrueNAS does not store it); use KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL.

**Credential (credential_type and its fields):**

Active Directory and IPA (Kerberos only; the first join needs KERBEROS_USER with domain admin rights):
- KERBEROS_USER: {credential_type: "KERBEROS_USER", username: "admin", password: "pass"}
- KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL: {credential_type: "KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL", principal: "host/truenas@EXAMPLE.COM"} (the principal must already be in a keytab on TrueNAS)

LDAP (also accepts the Kerberos types above, which need kerberos_realm to be set):
- LDAP_PLAIN: {credential_type: "LDAP_PLAIN", binddn: "cn=admin,dc=example,dc=com", bindpw: "pass"}
- LDAP_ANONYMOUS: {credential_type: "LDAP_ANONYMOUS"}
- LDAP_MTLS: {credential_type: "LDAP_MTLS", client_certificate: "name of a certificate on TrueNAS"}

**Configuration (fields per service_type; * = required):**
- ACTIVEDIRECTORY: hostname*, domain*, site, computer_account_ou, use_default_domain, enable_trusted_domains, trusted_domains, idmap
  e.g. {hostname: "truenas", domain: "corp.example.com"}
- IPA: target_server*, hostname*, domain*, basedn*, smb_domain, validate_certificates
  e.g. {target_server: "ipa.example.com", hostname: "truenas", domain: "example.com", basedn: "dc=example,dc=com"}
- LDAP: server_urls* (ldap:// or ldaps:// URIs), basedn*, starttls, validate_certificates, schema (RFC2307 or RFC2307BIS), search_bases, attribute_maps, auxiliary_parameters
  e.g. {server_urls: ["ldaps://ldap.example.com"], basedn: "dc=example,dc=com"}
idmap, trusted_domains, smb_domain, search_bases and attribute_maps are passed to TrueNAS unchanged; see the TrueNAS API docs for directoryservices.update for their fields.

**Security:**
- Credentials are stored in TrueNAS configuration
- Use Kerberos principals with keytabs instead of passwords for production
- Dry-run shows the exact payload that would be sent with every secret value masked (password, bindpw, ldap_user_dn_password in idmap and trusted_domains, ...); credential_type and username stay visible

**Returns:** task_id for tracking the long-running domain join job (2-10 minutes typical) **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

configuration.description: service_type specific configuration; see the tool description for the fields of each service type and which are required

attribute_maps.description: LDAP: attribute mappings for non-standard servers, passed to TrueNAS unchanged

auxiliary_parameters.description: LDAP: extra SSSD parameters (not validated by TrueNAS)

basedn.description: IPA, LDAP: base DN for LDAP operations (required)

computer_account_ou.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: OU in which the computer account is created on first join

enable_trusted_domains.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: support trusted domains (set trusted_domains too)

hostname.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY, IPA: hostname TrueNAS registers in the domain (required)

idmap.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: idmap settings (builtin and idmap_domain), passed to TrueNAS unchanged

schema.description: LDAP: attribute schema of the server

search_bases.description: LDAP: base_user, base_group and base_netgroup search bases, passed to TrueNAS unchanged

server_urls.description: LDAP: server URIs beginning with ldap:// or ldaps:// (required)

site.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: Active Directory site (detected automatically when omitted)

smb_domain.description: IPA: SMB domain settings, passed to TrueNAS unchanged

target_server.description: IPA: name of the IPA server used when joining or leaving (required)

trusted_domains.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: idmap configuration for each trusted domain

use_default_domain.description: ACTIVEDIRECTORY: drop the domain prefix from user and group names

validate_certificates.description: IPA, LDAP: validate the directory server's certificates (TrueNAS default: true)

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

credential.description: Credential used to bind to the directory service. credential_type selects the other fields: KERBEROS_USER (username, password), KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL (principal), LDAP_PLAIN (binddn, bindpw), LDAP_ANONYMOUS (none), LDAP_MTLS (client_certificate). LDAP_* types are only valid for service_type LDAP.

binddn.description: LDAP_PLAIN: distinguished name to bind as

bindpw.description: LDAP_PLAIN: password of the bind DN

client_certificate.description: LDAP_MTLS: name of the client certificate on TrueNAS

principal.description: KERBEROS_PRINCIPAL: principal present in a keytab on TrueNAS

username.description: KERBEROS_USER: account used to obtain a Kerberos ticket

enable.description: Enable the service (true joins the domain the first time; false disables it but keeps the settings)

enable_account_cache.description: Cache user and group lists (TrueNAS default: true; omit to keep the current value)

enable_dns_updates.description: Automatic DNS updates via nsupdate (TrueNAS default: true; omit to keep the current value)

force.description: Skip the check for an existing server registered with the same hostname in the domain. Can replace that server; do not use casually.

kerberos_realm.description: Kerberos realm used to authenticate to the directory service. Required for Kerberos credentials with service_type LDAP; detected automatically when first joining AD or IPA.

service_type.description: Directory service type. Selects which configuration fields apply.

timeout.description: DNS query and LDAP request timeout in seconds (5-60; TrueNAS default: 10)

name: create_dataset
description:
Create a ZFS dataset (filesystem or volume) for storage. This tool is reusable for SMB shares, NFS exports, iSCSI LUNs, and application storage. Supports native ZFS encryption (encryption=true with encryption_options), compression, quotas, and advanced ZFS features.

**WIZARD GUIDANCE FOR LLM:**
When helping users create datasets, ask these questions in order:

1. **Pool Selection**: Query available pools first, ask which pool to use
2. **Dataset Name**: Suggest format 'pool/shares/name' or 'pool/apps/name'
3. **Dataset Type**: FILESYSTEM (default, for files) or VOLUME (for block storage/VMs)
4. **Share Type Optimization** (if for sharing):
   - SMB: Windows/Mac file shares (recommend for SMB shares)
   - NFS: Unix/Linux file shares
   - MULTIPROTOCOL: Both SMB and NFS access
   - APPS: Application storage
   - GENERIC: General purpose (default)
5. **Encryption** (recommend for sensitive data):
   - Ask: "Is this for sensitive data?"
   - If yes: set encryption=true and encryption_options with exactly ONE method; ask which the user wants and do not default to one: generate_key=true, passphrase (8-512 bytes) or key (64 hex characters). encryption_options without encryption=true is rejected
   - generate_key: TrueNAS stores the key in its key database and does not return it; this tool cannot export it, so tell the user to back it up in the TrueNAS web UI (Datasets > select the dataset > Encryption > Export Key) and keep a copy somewhere other than this system
   - passphrase: TrueNAS does not store it; if it is lost the data is lost
   - key: the user must keep it; this tool does not return or recover it
   - Under a passphrase-encrypted parent, the new dataset must use a passphrase (TrueNAS refuses generate_key and key there)
   - The algorithm is not configurable through this tool; new encrypted datasets use AES-256-GCM
6. **Compression**: LZ4 (recommended, balanced), ZSTD (modern), GZIP (higher compression), OFF
7. **Space Quota** (optional): Ask if they want to limit size
8. **ACL Type** (for SMB): NFSV4 (recommended for SMB/Windows), POSIX (Unix)
9. **Advanced** (usually skip unless user asks):
   - Deduplication: Warn about RAM overhead, recommend OFF
   - Checksum, snapdir, atime, readonly

**IMPORTANT RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- For SMB shares: share_type=SMB, acltype=NFSV4, compression=LZ4
- For NFS exports: share_type=NFS, acltype=POSIX, compression=LZ4
- For multi-protocol: share_type=MULTIPROTOCOL, acltype=NFSV4
- For apps: share_type=APPS, compression=LZ4 or ZSTD
- Always recommend compression=LZ4 unless user has specific needs
- Warn: Deduplication uses ~5GB RAM per TB, not recommended for most users
- Warn: Encryption cannot be removed later, only option is to copy data elsewhere

**BEFORE EXECUTING:**
1. Use dry_run=true to preview the configuration
2. Display summary showing: name, type, optimization, compression, encryption, quota, mountpoint
3. Get explicit user confirmation with "Shall I proceed?"
4. Warn: This is a WRITE operation creating permanent storage
5. If encryption enabled, remind the user of the key-backup note for the chosen method after creation

**DRY RUN:**
Set dry_run=true to preview what will be created without executing. The preview's ancestors_to_create lists any missing parent datasets that would be created (create_ancestors defaults to true), from parent to child. Those ancestors are created with no properties of their own; they inherit compression, ACL type and encryption from their parent and have no quota of their own, and do not receive this dataset's share_type, compression or encryption. Under an unencrypted parent, ancestors of an encrypted dataset are unencrypted. The preview fails if the pool does not exist, the dataset already exists, or the name is invalid. Show user the preview, then ask for confirmation to proceed.

acltype.description: NFSV4 (recommended for SMB/Windows ACLs) or POSIX (Unix permissions)

atime.description: File access time tracking: ON or OFF (OFF improves performance)

checksum.description: Data integrity algorithm: SHA256 (default), BLAKE3, SHA512, etc.

compression.description: LZ4 (recommended, balanced), ZSTD (modern), GZIP (higher compression), OFF, or INHERIT (default)

create_ancestors.description: Auto-create missing parent datasets (default: true). A dry-run preview lists any missing ancestors that would be created, from parent to child, in ancestors_to_create. Those ancestors inherit compression, ACL type and encryption from their parent and have no quota of their own

deduplication.description: OFF (recommended), ON, or VERIFY. Warning: Uses ~5GB RAM per TB of storage

dry_run.description: Preview what will be created without executing (default: false)

encryption.description: Create the dataset as a new ZFS encryption root (cannot be removed later). Requires encryption_options. inherit_encryption is sent as false automatically; passing inherit_encryption=true with this is rejected

encryption_options.description: Key material for a new encrypted dataset; only valid together with encryption=true. Provide exactly one of generate_key=true, passphrase or key. The passphrase and key are secrets and are masked in dry-run output

generate_key.description: Let TrueNAS generate the key and store it in its key database; it is not returned. This tool cannot export it: back it up in the TrueNAS web UI (Datasets > select the dataset > Encryption > Export Key) and keep a copy elsewhere. Refused under a passphrase-encrypted parent

key.description: Raw encryption key as exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. You must keep a copy; this tool never returns it. Refused under a passphrase-encrypted parent

passphrase.description: Passphrase of 8 to 512 bytes. It is not stored by TrueNAS: if it is lost the data is lost

pbkdf2iters.description: PBKDF2 iterations for a passphrase (optional; only with passphrase; minimum 100000, TrueNAS 27.0 requires at least 1300000). Omit to use the TrueNAS default

inherit_encryption.description: Optional. Whether the dataset inherits the parent's encryption settings (TrueNAS default: true). false asks for an unencrypted dataset, which TrueNAS rejects under an encrypted parent. To create a new encrypted dataset use encryption=true with encryption_options instead (inherit_encryption is then sent as false automatically); inherit_encryption=true together with encryption=true is rejected

quota.description: Maximum space for dataset + children in bytes (e.g., 1099511627776 for 1TB)

refquota.description: Maximum space for dataset only (excluding children) in bytes

share_type.description: Optimization hint: GENERIC (default), SMB, NFS, MULTIPROTOCOL, APPS

snapdir.description: Snapshot directory visibility: VISIBLE or HIDDEN

type.description: FILESYSTEM (default, for files/directories) or VOLUME (for block storage/iSCSI/VMs)

user_properties.description: Optional ZFS user properties to set on the dataset, each an object with a 'key' containing a colon in namespace:property form (e.g. 'org:note') and a string 'value'. Property names should use only lowercase letters, digits and ': . _ -' (newer TrueNAS versions reject anything else) and must not repeat within the list. Do not set properties TrueNAS manages itself (org.freenas:description, org.freenas:quota_warning, org.freenas:quota_critical, org.freenas:refquota_warning, org.freenas:refquota_critical, org.truenas:managedby); use the dedicated fields (comments, quota_warning, ...) instead

key.description: User property name in namespace:property form; must contain a colon, e.g. 'org:note'

volblocksize.description: VOLUME type only (rejected for FILESYSTEM): volume block size. Defaults to 16K, or 128K on a dRAID pool

volsize.description: Required for VOLUME type: size in bytes (e.g., 1099511627776 for 1TB)

name: create_nfs_share
description:
Create an NFS (Network File System) share for Unix/Linux file sharing. This makes a ZFS dataset accessible over the network via the NFS protocol.

**WIZARD GUIDANCE FOR LLM:**
When helping users create NFS shares, follow this conversation flow:

**1. Dataset Selection:**
- Ask: "Do you want to create a new dataset or use an existing ZFS dataset?"
- If NEW: Use create_dataset tool first (with share_type=NFS, acltype=POSIX)
- If EXISTING: 
  * Query available datasets first with query_datasets
  * Present options to user (NEVER suggest pool root like 'tank' or 'flash')
  * Use the dataset's mountpoint as the path
  * Warn: "Never share a pool root - always use a child dataset"
- After dataset creation, use its mountpoint as the path

**2. Access Control:**
- Ask: "Read-only or read-write?" (default: read-write)
- Ask: "Restrict to specific networks?" (CIDR notation: 192.168.1.0/24)
- Ask: "Restrict to specific hosts?" (IP addresses or hostnames)
- Recommend: At least one restriction (network or host) for security

**3. User Mapping (Important for Security):**
- Ask: "How should root access be handled?"
  * **maproot_user**: Map root clients to specific user (recommended: 'nobody')
  * **maproot_group**: Map root clients to specific group (recommended: 'nogroup')
  * Warn if not set: "Root clients will have full root access (security risk)"
- Ask: "Map all users to a specific user?" (optional, for anonymous access)
  * **mapall_user**: Maps all clients to one user
  * **mapall_group**: Maps all client groups to one group

**4. Security Level (Optional):**
- Default: SYS (system authentication)
- Advanced: KRB5, KRB5I, KRB5P (Kerberos, requires setup)
- Usually skip unless user specifically needs Kerberos

**IMPORTANT RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- For NFS shares: share_type=NFS, acltype=POSIX (in dataset creation)
- Compression: LZ4 recommended for balanced performance
- Always set maproot_user='nobody' to prevent root access
- Use network/host restrictions to limit access
- Read-only for shared data that shouldn't be modified

**SECURITY WARNINGS TO DISPLAY:**
- If no network/host restrictions: "Share accessible from any host"
- If no maproot_user: "Root clients will have full root access"
- If read-write + no restrictions: "Any host can modify/delete files"
- Remind: "Ensure NFS service is running and firewall allows NFS traffic (port 2049)"

**BEFORE EXECUTING:**
1. Use dry_run=true to preview the configuration
2. Display complete summary including:
   - Local path
   - Access type (read-only/read-write)
   - Network/host restrictions
   - User mapping settings
   - Security warnings if applicable
3. Get explicit user confirmation: "Shall I create this NFS share?"
4. Warn: "This is a WRITE operation that exposes data over your network"
5. After creation: Provide mount command example

**DRY RUN:**
Set dry_run=true to preview what will be created without executing. Show user the preview including security warnings, then ask for confirmation.

dry_run.description: Preview what will be created without executing (default: false)

enabled.description: Enable share for network access (default: true)

hosts.description: Authorized IP addresses or hostnames (e.g., ['192.168.1.10', 'client.local']). No quotes or spaces. Empty = allow all hosts.

mapall_group.description: Map all client groups to this group (optional, for anonymous access)

mapall_user.description: Map all clients to this user (optional, for anonymous access)

maproot_group.description: Map root clients to this group (recommended: 'nogroup' for security)

maproot_user.description: Map root clients to this user (recommended: 'nobody' for security)

networks.description: Authorized networks in CIDR notation (e.g., ['192.168.1.0/24']). Empty = allow all networks.

path.description: ZFS dataset mountpoint starting with /mnt/ (e.g., /mnt/tank/shares/data, NOT /mnt/tank)

name: create_scrub_schedule
description: Create automated scrub schedule for a pool. **Best practices**: Schedule weekly for production, monthly for home use. Run during off-peak hours (2-4am typical). Scrubs can take hours/days on large pools but are essential for data integrity.

pool.description: Required: Pool name to schedule scrubs for

schedule.description: Required: Cron schedule (e.g., {minute: '0', hour: '2', dow: '0'} for Sunday 2am)

name: create_smb_share
description:
Create an SMB (Windows/macOS file sharing) share. This makes a ZFS dataset accessible over the network via the SMB/CIFS protocol.

**WIZARD GUIDANCE FOR LLM:**
When helping users create SMB shares, follow this conversation flow:

**1. Dataset Selection:**
- Ask: "Do you want to create a new dataset or use an existing ZFS dataset?"
- If NEW: Use create_dataset tool first (with share_type=SMB, acltype=NFSV4)
- If EXISTING: 
  * Query available datasets first with query_datasets
  * Present options to user (NEVER suggest pool root like 'tank' or 'flash')
  * Use the dataset's mountpoint as the path
  * Warn: "Never share a pool root - always use a child dataset"
- After dataset creation, use its mountpoint as the path

**2. Share Name:**
- Ask: "What name should appear when browsing the network?"
- Rules: Max 80 chars, no \ / [ ] : | < > + = ; , * ? "
- Cannot use: global, printers, homes
- Suggest: Use a friendly, descriptive name like "TeamDocs" or "PhotoArchive"

**3. Description:**
- Ask: "Add a description?" (optional, shown when browsing shares)

**4. Purpose Selection:**
- Ask: "What's this share for?"
- Options:
  * DEFAULT_SHARE: Standard file sharing (most common)
  * TIMEMACHINE_SHARE: macOS Time Machine backups
  * MULTIPROTOCOL_SHARE: Both SMB and NFS access (complex permissions)
  * PRIVATE_DATASETS_SHARE: User home directories
  * VEEAM_REPOSITORY_SHARE: Veeam backup storage
- Recommend DEFAULT_SHARE unless specific use case

**5. Access Control:**
- Ask: "Read-only or read-write?" (default: read-write)
- Ask: "Should it be visible when browsing?" (default: yes)
- Ask: "Restrict to specific IP addresses?" (optional, for hostsallow)
- Ask: "Hide from unauthorized users?" (access_based_share_enumeration)

**6. Purpose-Specific Questions:**

For TIMEMACHINE_SHARE:
- Ask: "What's the backup size limit?" (recommend 2-3x Mac's disk size)
- Set time_machine_quota in options

For MULTIPROTOCOL_SHARE:
- Warn: "Multi-protocol shares have complex permission interactions"
- Recommend: "Use either SMB OR NFS, not both, unless you understand the implications"

For PRIVATE_DATASETS_SHARE:
- Suggest: "Create separate datasets per user for isolation"
- Recommend: "Use access_based_share_enumeration=true"

**7. Auditing (Optional):**
- Ask: "Enable access auditing?" (tracks who accesses files)
- If yes: Ask which groups to audit (empty = audit all)

**IMPORTANT RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Default: enabled=true, browsable=true, readonly=false
- For sensitive data: Set access_based_share_enumeration=true
- For public shares: Use hostsdeny to block unwanted networks
- For Time Machine: Set appropriate quota to prevent filling pool
- For multi-protocol: Strongly recommend against unless necessary

**SECURITY WARNINGS TO DISPLAY:**
- If browsable=true + no hostsallow: "Share visible and accessible from any network"
- If readonly=false: "Users can modify, delete, and create files"
- If no access restrictions: "Anyone on your network can access this share"
- Remind: "Configure share permissions in TrueNAS UI after creation"

**BEFORE EXECUTING:**
1. Use dry_run=true to preview the configuration
2. Display complete summary including:
   - Share name and network path (\\truenas\sharename)
   - Local path
   - Purpose and access settings
   - Security warnings if applicable
3. Get explicit user confirmation: "Shall I create this share?"
4. Warn: "This is a WRITE operation that exposes data over your network"
5. After creation: Remind user to configure permissions via TrueNAS UI

**DRY RUN:**
Set dry_run=true to preview what will be created without executing. Show user the preview including security warnings, then ask for confirmation.

access_based_share_enumeration.description: Hide share from users without filesystem ACL access (default: false)

audit.description: Audit configuration for tracking file access

browsable.description: Show share in network browse lists (default: true)

comment.description: Description shown when clients list shares (optional)

dry_run.description: Preview what will be created without executing (default: false)

enabled.description: Enable share for network access (default: true)

hostsallow.description: IP addresses/networks allowed to access (empty = allow all)

hostsdeny.description: IP addresses/networks denied access (empty = deny none)

name.description: Share name visible to clients (max 80 chars, case-insensitive, must be unique)

path.description: ZFS dataset mountpoint starting with /mnt/ (e.g., /mnt/tank/shares/docs, NOT /mnt/tank). Use 'EXTERNAL' only for DFS proxy shares.

purpose.description: Share purpose: DEFAULT_SHARE (standard), TIMEMACHINE_SHARE (macOS backups), MULTIPROTOCOL_SHARE (SMB+NFS), PRIVATE_DATASETS_SHARE (home dirs)

readonly.description: Prevent clients from creating/modifying files (default: false)

name: delete_app
description: Remove an installed application. IMPORTANT: Host-path datasets are NOT deleted and must be manually removed after app deletion. Data will be preserved in original locations. Use dry-run mode to preview what will be deleted. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

name: delete_boot_environment
description: Delete a boot environment by name. Supports dry-run mode to preview deletion and show warnings. Safety checks prevent deleting active/activated/protected environments. **IMPORTANT**: This operation is permanent and irreversible. Recommend keeping at least 2-3 boot environments for system recovery. Always use dry-run first to verify it is safe to delete. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

dry_run.description: Preview what will be deleted without executing (default: false)

id.description: Required: Boot environment name to delete

description: Remove a scrub schedule. **IMPORTANT**: Pool will no longer have automatic scrubbing. Recommend running manual scrubs monthly if schedule is deleted. Consider updating schedule instead of deleting. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

name: dismiss_alert
description: Dismiss a system alert by UUID

dry_run.description: Preview without changing the alert (default: false)

name: download_update
description: Download TrueNAS system update. Supports dry-run mode to preview changes. Returns a task ID for tracking download progress. This is a write operation.

train.description: Optional train name passed to update.download. Must be set together with version, or both omitted. When both are omitted, the download uses the update offered by the system's configured profile

version.description: Optional version passed to update.download. Must be set together with train, or both omitted

name: get_app_catalog_details
description:
Get detailed information about a specific app from the catalog, including README, screenshots, version info, storage volume hints, and the app schema (groups and questions, with each question's defaults). When the schema defines run-as user/group or resource limits, those defaults are included in a defaults object; they are omitted when the schema has none. The defaults object uses the schema's own nesting (for example defaults.resources.limits.cpus and defaults.resources.limits.memory); put those values under the same keys in install_app values. When the schema has run_as_custom_user, the run_as defaults apply only if that flag is true and are omitted from defaults when its default is false. When the schema has enable_resource_limits, the resources.limits defaults apply only if that flag is true and are omitted from defaults when its default is false.

Before calling install_app: review every schema group, call query_pools and ask the user which pool to use if more than one is available (use the only pool if there is just one), create datasets with create_dataset, and set every storage volume to type host_path under /mnt/<pool>/.... Use the schema's own defaults for run-as and resources when they are present. This result describes the app and its schema; it does not issue client-specific instructions.

app_name.description: App name from catalog (from search results)

train.description: Catalog train (optional). When omitted, the train that has the app is looked up in the catalog; if several do, stable is preferred, then enterprise, then community. The response reports the train used.

name: get_app_config
description: Retrieve the current user-specified configuration for an installed app. Returns the values object that can be modified and passed to update_app.

name: get_arc_metrics
description: Get ZFS ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache) reporting metrics such as ARC size. Which ARC graphs exist depends on the TrueNAS version; the supported set is discovered from the server.

graphs.description: ARC graphs to retrieve, e.g. 'arcsize'. Other ARC graphs are accepted when the server supports them. Default: every ARC graph the server supports.

name: get_current_boot_environment
description: Get current boot environment status. Shows which boot environment is currently running (active) and which will boot on next restart (activated). Quick reference tool before making system changes.

name: get_directory_service_status
description: Get current directory service status and health. Returns service type (ACTIVEDIRECTORY, IPA, LDAP), status (DISABLED, HEALTHY, FAULTED, JOINING, LEAVING), and error messages if any. Use for quick health checks.

name: get_disk_metrics
description: Get disk performance metrics (I/O or temperature)

disk.description: Disk name (e.g., 'sda'). If omitted, returns all disks.

type.description: Metric type: disk I/O or disk temperature (default: disk)

name: get_network_metrics
description: Get network interface traffic metrics

interface.description: Network interface name (e.g., 'eth0'). If omitted, returns all interfaces.

name: get_pool_capacity_details
description: Get detailed pool and dataset capacity information with utilization analysis. Returns current capacity snapshot with breakdown by dataset. Note: Historical capacity trends are not available from TrueNAS API; use Netdata graphs if available.

name: get_scrub_status
description: Get comprehensive scrub status for all pools. Combines schedule information, current scrub progress, and last scrub results. Use this to answer questions like 'when was tank last scrubbed?' or 'is a scrub running?' An empty pool name is treated as unset and returns every pool.

pool.description: Optional: Specific pool name (omit or pass an empty string for all pools)

name: get_system_metrics
description: Get system performance metrics (CPU, memory, load average, CPU temperature, uptime)

graphs.description: Metrics to retrieve (default: cpu, memory, load)

name: get_ups_metrics
description: Get UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) metrics. For upsvoltage, returns battery, input, and output voltage. Requires a UPS configured in TrueNAS.

name: install_app
description:
Install a TrueNAS application using schema-driven configuration.

**IMPORTANT: ALL TRUENAS APPS ARE COMPLEX**
Every app requires configuration across multiple groups (currently 6, but may vary):
1. App Configuration (timezone, app-specific settings)
2. User and Group Configuration (run_as user/group IDs)
3. Network Configuration (ports and networking)
4. Storage Configuration (volumes and datasets)
5. Labels Configuration (metadata labels)
6. Resources Configuration (CPU, memory, GPU)

**UNIVERSAL WIZARD - SECTION-BY-SECTION CONFIGURATION:**

**STEP 1: Get App Schema**
1. Call get_app_catalog_details(app_name, train)
2. Review schema.groups array (iterate through ALL groups, don't assume count)
3. Check schema.group_count to know how many groups to configure
4. Review schema.questions_by_group (shows questions for each group)
5. Use the schema's own defaults for run-as and resources when they are present; omit them when the schema has none

**STEP 2: Understand Common Patterns**

All apps follow these patterns:

• **Timezone** (Group 1):
  - Variable: TZ
  - Type: enum with 600+ timezones
  - Recommendation: Use "Etc/UTC" or user's timezone

• **User/Group** (Group 2):
  - Variable: run_as
  - Structure: {user: <uid>, group: <gid>}
  - Defaults: take user and group from the app schema when present; omit them when the schema has none

• **Network** (Group 3):
  - Variable: network
  - Ports: {bind_mode: "published", port_number: <port>, host_ips: []}
  - Common ports: web_port, api_port, sync_port, etc.
  - bind_mode: "published" (external) or "exposed" (internal) or "" (none)

• **Storage** (Group 4) - CRITICAL:
  - Variable: storage
  - ALWAYS use: {"type": "host_path", "host_path_config": {"path": "/mnt/...", "acl_enable": false}}
  - NEVER use: {"type": "ix_volume", ...}
  - Common volumes: config, cache, data, transcodes
  - Pattern: /mnt/<pool>/apps/<appname>/<volume>

• **Labels** (Group 5):
  - Variable: labels
  - Structure: [{key: "name", value: "value"}]
  - Usually optional (empty array)

• **Resources** (Group 6):
  - Variable: resources
  - Structure: {limits: {cpus: <schema default>, memory: <schema default>}, gpus: {...}}
  - Defaults: take CPU and memory limits from the app schema when present; omit them when the schema has none

**STEP 3: Plan Storage (CRITICAL - Do This First)**

1. Identify storage volumes from schema:
   - Look in schema.questions_by_group["Storage Configuration"]
   - Find variables like: config, cache, data, transcodes, additional_storage
   - Each has type enum: ["host_path", "ix_volume", ...]

2. Call query_pools() to find available pools

3. Recommend dataset structure:
   - Format: <pool>/apps/<appname>/<volume>
   - Example: tank/apps/jellyfin/config

4. Present plan to user:
   "I'll create the following datasets for Jellyfin:
    - tank/apps/jellyfin/config (10GB)
    - tank/apps/jellyfin/cache (50GB)
    - tank/apps/jellyfin/transcodes (temporary, no dataset needed)"

**STEP 4: Create Datasets**

For each permanent storage volume (not temporary/tmpfs):
1. Call create_dataset with:
   - name: "<pool>/apps/<appname>/<volume>"
   - type: "FILESYSTEM"
   - share_type: "APPS"
   - compression: "LZ4"
   - quota: <size_in_bytes> (optional)
2. Confirm creation
3. Recommended quotas:
   - config: 10GB (10737418240)
   - cache: 50GB (53687091200)
   - data: 1TB+ (varies by app)

**STEP 5: Build Configuration by Group**

Go through each group and build configuration:

**Group 1 - App Configuration:**
{
  "TZ": "Etc/UTC",
  "<appname>": {
    // App-specific settings from schema
    "additional_envs": []
  }
}

**Group 2 - User/Group:**
{
  "run_as": {
    "user":  // from the app schema default, when present
    "group": // from the app schema default, when present
  }
}

**Group 3 - Network:**
{
  "network": {
    "web_port": {
      "bind_mode": "published",
      "port_number": 30013,
      "host_ips": []
    },
    "host_network": false
  }
}

**Group 4 - Storage (CRITICAL):**
{
  "storage": {
    "config": {
      "type": "host_path",
      "host_path_config": {
        "path": "/mnt/tank/apps/jellyfin/config",
        "acl_enable": false
      }
    },
    "cache": {
      "type": "host_path",
      "host_path_config": {
        "path": "/mnt/tank/apps/jellyfin/cache",
        "acl_enable": false
      }
    },
    "transcodes": {
      "type": "temporary"
    },
    "additional_storage": []
  }
}

**Group 5 - Labels:**
{
  "labels": []
}

**Group 6 - Resources:**
{
  "resources": {
    "limits": {
      "cpus":   // from the app schema default, when present
      "memory": // from the app schema default, when present
    },
    "gpus": {}
  }
}

**STEP 6: Assemble Complete Values Object**

Combine all groups into single values object:
{
  "TZ": "Etc/UTC",
  "jellyfin": {...},
  "run_as": {...},
  "network": {...},
  "storage": {...},
  "labels": [...],
  "resources": {...}
}

**STEP 7: Validate Configuration**

1. All storage volumes use type="host_path"
2. All paths start with /mnt/
3. All required groups present
4. Port numbers in valid range (1-65535)
5. User/group IDs are valid (>= 0)

**STEP 8: Dry-Run Preview**

Call install_app with dry_run=true:
install_app(
  app_name="jellyfin",
  catalog_app="jellyfin",
  train="community",
  values={...complete config...},
  dry_run=true
)

Review:
- Datasets exist?
- Configuration valid?
- Warnings or errors?

**STEP 9: Execute Installation**

If dry-run successful, call with dry_run=false:
install_app(
  app_name="jellyfin",
  catalog_app="jellyfin",
  train="community",
  values={...complete config...},
  dry_run=false
)

Returns task_id for tracking progress with tasks_get.

**CRITICAL SAFETY RULES:**
- ALWAYS use "type": "host_path" for storage
- NEVER use "type": "ix_volume"
- ALWAYS create datasets before installation
- ALWAYS validate paths start with /mnt/
- ALWAYS use dry-run before final installation

**ERROR RECOVERY:**
- Missing datasets: Create with create_dataset
- ix_volume detected: Convert to host_path format
- Invalid structure: Review schema and rebuild section
- Validation failed: Check error message for exact location

app_name.description: Unique app instance name (lowercase, alphanumeric, hyphens, 1-40 chars). Pattern: ^[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$

train.description: Catalog train (optional). When omitted, the train that has the catalog app is looked up; if several do, stable is preferred, then enterprise, then community. The response reports the train used.

values.description: Complete app configuration assembled from schema groups. Includes TZ, run_as, network, storage (host_path only), labels, and resources. Build this by iterating through schema groups from get_app_catalog_details.

name: leave_directory_service
description:
Leave the Active Directory or IPA domain TrueNAS has joined, with TrueNAS directoryservices.leave (TrueNAS 25.10 or later).

TrueNAS removes its computer account from the domain using the credential you provide, then resets its local directory service configuration and disables the service. LDAP cannot be left; use configure_directory_service with enable=false to disable it.

**credential is required:** a KERBEROS_USER credential, {credential_type: "KERBEROS_USER", username: "admin", password: "pass"}, for an account with the administrative privileges needed to remove the computer account. It is used for this operation only and is never shown: the password is masked in the dry run and in stored task data.

**WARNING:** This is a destructive operation:
- Removes TrueNAS from the domain
- Clears all cached user/group data
- All domain user authentication will stop working
- SMB/NFS shares configured with domain users will become inaccessible

**Alternative:** Use configure_directory_service with enable=false for temporary disable without leaving the domain.

**Returns:** task_id for tracking the leave job (30 seconds to 5 minutes typical) **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

credential.description: KERBEROS_USER credential used to remove the computer account from the domain

credential_type.description: Must be KERBEROS_USER, the only credential type directoryservices.leave accepts

username.description: Account used to obtain a Kerberos ticket; it must exist on the domain controller

dry_run.description: Preview operation without executing (default: false, STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to use dry_run first)

name: list_alerts
description: List system alerts. By default only active alerts are listed: dismissed alerts are excluded. Set include_dismissed=true to list all alerts, or dismissed=true to list only dismissed ones. Returns allow-listed alert fields (uuid, level, text, and so on). The middleware dedup key is omitted because it would be masked by output redaction; use uuid with dismiss_alert or restore_alert.

dismissed.description: Filter by dismissed status (true=dismissed only, false=active only, omit=active only unless include_dismissed=true)

include_dismissed.description: Also list dismissed alerts when dismissed is not set (default: false, dismissed alerts are excluded)

name: list_directory_certificates
description: List available certificates for LDAP MTLS authentication. Returns certificate IDs and names that can be used with LDAP_MTLS credential type.

name: query_apps
description: Query installed applications with their status, versions, and available updates. upgrade_available tells whether an upgrade exists; latest_version is the newest catalog version (always set, in catalog form, not comparable to human_version)

app_name.description: Optional: Filter by specific app name

name: query_boot_environments
description: Query TrueNAS boot environments with optional filtering and sorting. Returns simplified boot environment information showing which are active/activated/protected/deletable. Use 'limit' to control result size, 'order_by' to sort. Perfect for questions like 'what old boot environments can I clean up?' or 'which boot environment am I running?'

limit.description: Optional: Maximum number of boot environments to return (default: 50 for manageable response size)

name.description: Optional: Filter by boot environment name (partial match)

order_by.description: Optional: Sort by 'name' (alphabetical), 'created' (newest first, default), or 'size' (largest first)

show_deletable_only.description: Optional: Show only boot environments that are safe to delete (default: false)

show_protected_only.description: Optional: Show only protected (keep=true) boot environments (default: false)

name: query_datasets
description: Query datasets with optional filtering and sorting. Returns simplified dataset information with capacity, encryption status, and usage details. Use 'limit' to control result size (default: 50, maximum: 1000), 'order_by' to sort by size, and 'encrypted_only' to filter.

encrypted_only.description: Optional: Return only encrypted datasets (default: false)

limit.description: Optional: Maximum number of datasets to return (default: 50, maximum: 1000)

order_by.description: Optional: Sort by 'used' (space usage), 'available', or 'name' (default: used descending)

pool.description: Optional: Filter datasets by pool name (exact match; tank does not include tank2)

name: query_directory_services
description: Query full directory service configuration. Returns service type, enabled status, credentials (masked for security), and service-specific settings. All passwords and keytabs are masked in output.

name: query_jobs
description: Query system jobs (running, pending, or completed tasks like replication, snapshots, scrubs, app upgrades, etc.), most recent first. Returns jobs in every state unless state is given; method narrows to one job method (e.g. app.upgrade). state is case-insensitive, including all; with no state or all the response reports state_filter "ALL". Reports has_more and total when the list was cut by limit; long results and error text are truncated with a flag. A job state of SUCCESS means the job finished, not that the app or service it acted on is healthy: an app embedded in a job result is a copy from when the job ended. Use tasks_get or query_apps for the current app state.

limit.description: Maximum number of jobs to return (default: 50). The response has has_more (and total, the number of jobs matching the state and method filters) when more exist than were returned. Each job entry is at most 4 KiB. Must be an integer from 1 to 9999; other values are rejected with an error and nothing is queried.

method.description: Optional: only return jobs whose method is exactly this name, e.g. app.upgrade or pool.scrub.scrub

state.description: Filter by job state: RUNNING, WAITING, SUCCESS, FAILED, ABORTED or all, case-insensitive (default: all states; all is reported as state_filter "ALL")

name: query_pools
description: Query storage pools with their status, capacity, and health information. Returns allow-listed pool fields, RAIDZ expansion progress, a compact topology (type, path, name, guid, status, disk, device, and trimmed read/write/checksum error stats), and a trimmed scrub/resilver scan; it does not pass through the raw middleware record.

name: query_scrub_schedules
description: Query configured scrub schedules for all pools. Scrubs verify data integrity by reading all blocks and checking checksums, detecting and repairing silent corruption. Use filtering to view specific pools or only enabled schedules.

enabled_only.description: Optional: Show only enabled schedules (default: false)

pool.description: Optional: Filter by pool name (exact match)

name: query_shares
description: Query SMB and NFS shares configuration. Returns allow-listed share fields (including hostsallow/hostsdeny and NFS maps); extra middleware keys such as auxsmbconf are omitted.

share_type.description: Type of shares to query (default: all)

name: query_snapshots
description: Query ZFS snapshots with optional filtering and sorting. Returns simplified snapshot information with creation info, sizes and dataset. Holds are included only with 'include_holds' or 'holds_only' (they cost an extra lookup per snapshot). Use 'limit' to control result size (default: 50, maximum: 1000), 'order_by' to sort.

dataset.description: Optional: Filter snapshots by parent dataset name

holds_only.description: Optional: Return only snapshots with holds that prevent deletion (default: false). Implies include_holds.

include_holds.description: Optional: Include each snapshot's holds (default: false; one extra lookup per snapshot on the NAS)

limit.description: Optional: Maximum number of snapshots to return (default: 50, maximum: 1000)

order_by.description: Optional: Sort by 'name' (snapshot name, default descending), 'dataset' (parent dataset), or 'created' (parsed from name if available)

pool.description: Optional: Filter snapshots by pool name

name: query_vms
description: Query virtual machines with optional filtering and sorting. Returns simplified VM information with resource allocation, status, and device summary. Excludes sensitive data like display passwords.

limit.description: Optional: Maximum number of VMs to return (default: 50)

name.description: Optional: Filter VMs by name (partial match)

order_by.description: Optional: Sort by 'name' (default, alphabetical), 'memory' (descending), or 'status' (running first)

state.description: Optional: Filter by VM state (default: all)

name: refresh_directory_cache
description: Refresh cached user and group data from the directory service. Use after making changes in Active Directory, LDAP, or IPA that need to be reflected immediately in TrueNAS. Supports dry-run mode.

name: restore_alert
description: Restore (un-dismiss) a previously dismissed alert by UUID

dry_run.description: Preview without changing the alert (default: false)

uuid.description: UUID of the alert to restore

name: run_scrub
description: Manually start an immediate scrub on a pool. Returns a task ID for progress tracking when a scrub starts. Only ONLINE or DEGRADED pools are accepted. If the last scrub finished less than (threshold-1) days ago (default threshold 7, so under 6 days), returns scrub_started: false and does not start a scrub. **When to use**: Before critical backups, after hardware changes, when scheduled scrub was missed. Safe to run anytime but adds I/O load. Can be safely interrupted and resumed.

threshold.description: Optional: skip if the last scrub finished less than (N-1)*24h ago, matching TrueNAS (default: 7; 0 or 1 never skips)

name: search_app_catalog
description: Search TrueNAS app catalog by name, category, or keyword. Returns available applications from the catalog with their versions, categories, and installation status.

category.description: Filter by exact category name (the app's categories list must include this value, e.g. 'media', 'productivity', 'database')

query.description: Search query (case-insensitive literal substring match on the app name, not a regular expression)

train.description: Filter by catalog train (default: all trains). Each result includes its train.

name: start_app
description: Start a stopped TrueNAS application. Job-based; use tasks_get with returned task_id to track progress. Supports dry_run to preview the action without executing it.

app_name.description: Name of the application to start

dry_run.description: Preview the action without executing it (default: false)

name: stop_app
description: Stop a running TrueNAS application. Job-based; use tasks_get with returned task_id to track progress. Supports dry_run to preview the action without executing it. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

app_name.description: Name of the application to stop

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

dry_run.description: Preview the action without executing it (default: false)

name: system_health
description: Get system health status including alerts and diagnostics

name: system_info
description: Get TrueNAS system information including version, hostname, and platform details

name: system_reboot
description: Reboot the TrueNAS system. This will disconnect all active sessions and services. Use after applying system updates. Supports dry-run mode and an optional delay of up to 86400 seconds. A pending delayed reboot cannot be cancelled through this server. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

delay.description: Optional: seconds to wait before rebooting, 0-86400 (default: reboot immediately). Cannot be cancelled through this server once scheduled.

dry_run.description: Preview the reboot without executing (default: false)

name: tasks_get
description: Get the status of a task by ID: tool, job_id, status (working, completed, failed or cancelled), statusMessage and, once the job succeeded, its result (bounded; result_truncated is set when cut). If TrueNAS or its middleware restarts, the tracked job is gone and the task fails with a message naming the tool to check the state with. A task still working when its ttl (seconds since createdAt) runs out fails with "tracking timed out"; the operation may still be running. Finished tasks stay readable for 24 hours.

name: tasks_list
description: List tasks started by this server (newest first): running tasks, and finished ones for 24 hours after they finish (at most 500; the oldest finished are dropped first). Each task names the tool that started it (tool), the TrueNAS job it tracks (job_id), its status and statusMessage, and, once the job succeeded, its result (bounded; result_truncated is set when cut). Tasks are held in this server's memory only and are lost when it restarts.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return (default: 50)

name: update_app
description: Update an installed app's configuration. Job-based; use tasks_get with returned task_id to track progress. Use get_app_config first to retrieve current config, then pass modified values. Storage may be omitted to leave it unchanged, including existing ix_volume entries. A partial storage object has omitted slots filled from the current config before it is sent, so they do not revert to schema defaults. When a provided slot keeps the same type and location, omitted top-level keys (such as read_only) and omitted fields of host_path_config, nfs_config, and cifs_config are also filled from the current slot. New storage entries, and type or location changes that are not a same-type NFS or CIFS server/path change, must use host_path with a cleaned path under /mnt/<pool>/ on an existing dataset. Changing the type or location of an existing slot (including an NFS or CIFS server or path) requires allow_storage_change=true; the preview and confirmation name each changed slot and state that data is not migrated. A change to read_only or ACL settings (acl_enable or acl) on a slot whose type and location are unchanged does not need the flag, but is listed as a plan warning with the old and new values. Supports dry_run to preview changes. This is a write operation that modifies the system. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

allow_storage_change.description: Allow changing the type or location of an existing storage slot, including an NFS or CIFS server or path. Data is not migrated. Required when this update changes an existing slot's type or location. Not required for a read_only or ACL-only change (default: false).

app_name.description: Name of the installed application to update

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

values.description: Updated configuration values. Use get_app_config to retrieve current values first. Storage may be omitted to leave current storage unchanged. If a partial storage object is sent, omitted slots are filled from the current config before the update is submitted. When a provided slot keeps the same type and location, omitted top-level keys and omitted fields of host_path_config, nfs_config, and cifs_config are also filled from the current slot. New entries, and type or location changes that are not a same-type NFS or CIFS server/path change, must be host_path; unchanged existing entries, including ix_volume, are left as they are.

name: update_status
description: Get current TrueNAS system update status and progress

name: upgrade_app
description: Upgrade an application to a newer version. Supports dry-run mode to preview changes. Returns a task ID for tracking progress; the task completes only once the app is observed RUNNING after the upgrade job finishes (otherwise it fails with the app's state; if the app was merely still starting when health_timeout_seconds ran out, the message says the upgrade itself succeeded and the wait can be raised). For a version upgrade TrueNAS stops the app and snapshots its ix-volumes dataset (if it has one) for rollback; custom apps and image-only updates are instead redeployed with updated images, without a stop or any snapshot (the preview says which applies). A job state of SUCCESS only means the upgrade job finished, not that the app is healthy: use tasks_get or query_apps for the app state. Task IDs are kept in this server's memory only; after a server restart, list jobs with query_jobs (method app.upgrade narrows the list) and find the entry whose id matches the returned job_id. The changelog and version details shown come from the middleware's app.upgrade_summary and may be empty. This is a write operation that modifies the system. **DESTRUCTIVE: requires confirmation.** If the client supports MCP elicitation, the server asks the user to approve a short preview in the client and executes only if they accept. Otherwise it changes nothing and returns a preview plus a single-use confirmation_token, valid for 5 minutes and only for these exact arguments; after explicit approval, call again with the same arguments plus confirmation_token.

app_name.description: Name of the application to upgrade

confirmation_token.description: Required to execute. Omit it first: the server returns a preview and a confirmation_token and changes nothing. After the user has explicitly approved the preview, repeat the call with exactly the same arguments plus this token. Single use, valid for 5 minutes.

health_timeout_seconds.description: After the upgrade job finishes, how long to wait for the app to report RUNNING before the task fails (default: 60; 0 checks once without waiting). Must be an integer from 0 to 600, anything else is rejected. Raise it for slow-starting apps: running out of time while the app is still starting fails the task but does not mean the upgrade failed.

snapshot_hostpaths.description: Also request snapshots of the app's host paths before the upgrade (default: true for safety). This only affects host paths: for a version upgrade TrueNAS stops the app and snapshots its ix-volumes dataset (if it has one) regardless. It is ignored for custom apps and image-only updates, which take no snapshot. It is a request, not a confirmation: only host paths that are ZFS datasets are snapshotted and the upgrade job does not report which snapshots it took.
